rental_car_return_damage.title: Rental car: document damage on pickup and return, and know what the deposit is
rental_car_return_damage.summary: Take photos or video of the whole car, inside and out, at pickup and note every scratch in the handover protocol. Return it during opening hours with a staff member and ask for a return protocol. The deposit is blocked on a real credit card, usually in the name of the main driver, and debit cards are often refused. Consumer advice suggests full cover without excess. Information only.

bavaria_exam_deadlines.title: Bavaria: missing exam deadlines you are responsible for counts as failed
bavaria_exam_deadlines.summary: Under Art. 84 BayHIG, if students miss the deadlines for registering for or sitting an exam for reasons they are responsible for, the parts not taken in time count as taken and failed. Study regulations at universities of applied sciences can also treat the final exam as failed once the standard period is exceeded by two semesters. Check your own Prüfungsordnung and tell the exam office early if you have a valid reason.

credit_recognition_lisbon.title: Switching university: your credits must be recognised unless there is a substantial difference
credit_recognition_lisbon.summary: When you change university or course, the Lisbon Recognition Convention is the legal frame for recognising earlier modules. Recognition should happen unless there are essential differences in the competences, and the burden of proof is reversed: the university must show that the difference exists. You still have to cooperate with documents. Apply to the exam office of the new university.

whatsapp_contact_sync.title: WhatsApp and your address book: uploading contacts needs their consent
whatsapp_contact_sync.summary: WhatsApp reads your phone's address book and compares it with its database. Commentators argue that this upload of contacts' numbers needs consent from each contact. A 2017 ruling of the AG Bad Hersfeld made a parent liable for a child's phone in a family case. For purely private use the GDPR household exemption may apply, but businesses using WhatsApp with customer contacts face stricter duties. Information only.

online_review_deletion.title: Negative online reviews: false facts can be removed, opinions mostly stay
online_review_deletion.summary: A review can be removed if it states provably false facts or is an insult. Pure opinions are protected by free speech even if harsh, as long as they are not abuse. Courts distinguish between facts that can be proven and subjective views. The author has to prove a negative fact that is stated about someone. Information only.

ksk_student_freelancer.title: Künstlersozialkasse: freelance creatives, with a 3,900 euro yearly minimum
ksk_student_freelancer.summary: Self-employed artists and publicists (for example writers, musicians, designers or game designers) can be insured through the Künstlersozialkasse, which pays about half of the contributions through public money and clients' levy. Members generally need to earn at least 3,900 euro a year, with an exception for career starters in their first three years. Students need a matriculation certificate. Check eligibility with the KSK.

broadcast_fee_dorm_room.title: Dorm room: it counts as its own flat for the broadcasting fee if it has its own bell and mailbox
broadcast_fee_dorm_room.summary: A room in a student hall of residence counts as a separate flat for the Rundfunkbeitrag (18.36 euro a month, billed 55.08 euro per quarter) when it can be reached from a generally accessible corridor and has its own mailbox and bell. Then every room pays its own fee. Whether a dorm room counts as a single flat or as a shared flat is not always clear, so ask the Beitragsservice if you are unsure. BAföG recipients can apply for an exemption.

broadcast_fee_backdated.title: Broadcasting fee exemption: you can apply backdated for up to three years
broadcast_fee_backdated.summary: If you received BAföG (or a comparable benefit) and did not live with your parents, you can apply for the broadcasting fee exemption retroactively, at most for three years and only for the periods in which you actually got the benefit. The exemption only applies on application and only for the approval period, so you need to renew it. Hand in a copy of the BAföG notice; being poor by income alone is not enough.

cancel_button_no_detour.title: Cancel button: the confirmation page may not push you toward pausing instead
cancel_button_no_detour.summary: In July 2026 the BGH (I ZR 200/25, case against the gym chain FitX) decided that the page you land on after clicking the online cancellation button may not contain anything that distracts from cancelling. In the case, a prominent orange button offered to pause the contract instead, which was not allowed. The cancellation process has to be simple: no detours, no retention offers on the confirmation page. If a provider ignores the rules, the consumer protection association can act against it.

gym_special_termination.title: Gym: moving is no reason for early cancellation, long illness or long closure are
gym_special_termination.summary: A move, even for work, does not entitle you to cancel a gym contract early (BGH, 4 May 2016, XII ZR 62/15). A permanent illness that makes training impossible can justify an extraordinary cancellation, usually with a medical certificate, and so can a closure of the studio for several months. If the studio is closed for only about four weeks, a cancellation will probably not succeed, but you do not have to pay for the closed time. Send the cancellation in a provable way.

viewing_fee_agent_banned.title: Agent may not charge a viewing fee or extra charges for a rental flat
viewing_fee_agent_banned.summary: A landlord-side estate agent may not demand money from flat hunters for a viewing, registration, processing or similar extra charges. In a case before the Landgericht Stuttgart an agent asked 35 to 50 euro for each viewing; the court said no registration fees, expenses or other additional payments may be demanded on top of a commission. The commission itself is paid by whoever ordered the agent.

broker_fee_reclaim.title: Agent fee paid by mistake: you may be able to claim it back, up to three years
broker_fee_reclaim.summary: If you paid an estate agent's commission for a rental flat in breach of the Bestellerprinzip, you can refuse payment, and amounts already paid can be reclaimed for a limited time; the Berliner Mieterverein names three years. Demand the money back in writing with a deadline and keep the contract and payment proof. Association or lawyer advice helps if the agent refuses.

bike_night_clause.title: Bike insurance: check for a night-time clause (22:00-06:00)
bike_night_clause.summary: Many contents policies and bike policies contain a Nachtzeitklausel: between 22:00 and 06:00 the bike is only insured against theft if it is in your flat or a locked cellar or bike room. If your bike stands on the street at night and was stolen, the insurer may refuse. Look for this clause before you buy, and if possible choose a policy without it. Since nobody knows when it was stolen, the clause can lead to disputes.

pregnancy_dismissal_notice.title: Dismissed while pregnant: tell your employer within two weeks
pregnancy_dismissal_notice.summary: If you get a dismissal and you were pregnant at that time, you can inform the employer about your pregnancy within two weeks after receiving the notice, even if the employer did not know. This matters because pregnancy normally comes with special protection against dismissal. Do it in a provable way, for example with a doctor's certificate, and check the three-week deadline for a dismissal protection claim at the labour court separately.

reference_exclusion_period.title: Reference: contractual exclusion periods can also cut off a correction claim
reference_exclusion_period.summary: If your contract or a collective agreement has an exclusion period (Ausschlussfrist) for all claims from the employment, IG Metall says this also covers the claim to correct a reference. If you are unhappy with your reference, check the contract, ask for the correction in writing and do not wait too long. The claim to a reference as such is separate and can be lost by long delay.

heat_at_work.title: Heat at work: no right to Hitzefrei, but the employer must act from 30 degrees
heat_at_work.summary: There is no general legal right to Hitzefrei at work. The workplace rule ASR A3.5 sets steps: above 26 degrees room temperature the employer should check and take measures such as ventilation or shading, above 30 degrees effective measures are required (for example drinks, flexible hours, fans), and above 35 degrees a room is not suitable as a workplace without special protection. There is no claim to free drinks or air conditioning. Your employer's risk assessment decides the measures.

works_council_hearing.title: Works council: it must be heard before every dismissal, otherwise it is void
works_council_hearing.summary: A works council can be elected in establishments with at least five permanent employees entitled to vote. Part-timers and marginally employed staff count as voters. Before any dismissal the employer has to hear the works council and tell it the reasons; a dismissal without that hearing is invalid. In a company without a works council this protection does not exist, and the three-week deadline for the labour court still applies.

commuter_allowance_2026.title: Commuting allowance 2026: 38 cent per km from the first kilometre, students count too
commuter_allowance_2026.summary: From 1 January 2026 the Entfernungspauschale is 0.38 euro for each full kilometre of the one-way distance from the first kilometre on (before: 0.30 euro for the first 20 km). Full-time students generally have the university as their first place of work and can only use this flat rate for the way to the university. It only has an effect on tax if all your Werbungskosten exceed the 1,230 euro lump sum. For a dual study with a training contract, other rules can apply.

church_leave_bavaria.title: Leaving the church in Bavaria: at the registry office, with an appointment, tax ends afterwards
church_leave_bavaria.summary: In Bavaria you declare your Kirchenaustritt in person at the Standesamt (or in writing via a notary); in Munich the registry office takes visits by appointment only. It is effective when the correct declaration arrives at the office. A fee applies; one Bavarian town names 35 euro, so check the current fee. Church tax in Bavaria is 8 percent of income tax and ends with your membership. Keep the certificate for your tax return.

naturalisation_five_years.title: Naturalisation: five years of lawful residence, B1 German, secure income
naturalisation_five_years.summary: Since the 2024 reform you can apply for German citizenship after five years of lawful, habitual residence in Germany (before: eight) and dual citizenship is allowed. Conditions include German at B1, a naturalisation test, a secured livelihood without benefits and a declaration of loyalty to the constitution. The fast track after three years was abolished in autumn 2025. Check with your local Einbürgerungsbehörde how study years count in your case.

epa_opt_out.title: Electronic patient record (ePA): you get one automatically unless you object
epa_opt_out.summary: Since 15 January 2025 every person with statutory health insurance gets an electronic patient record (ePA für alle) unless they object (opt-out). You can object at any time through the ePA app or your health fund, and an existing record is then deleted. You can also block individual practices, hospitals or pharmacies or restrict single functions. From the 15th birthday you manage your own rights. Objecting has no disadvantage for your care.

erasure_request_gdpr.title: Erasure: ask a company to delete your data, they have one month to answer
erasure_request_gdpr.summary: Under Article 17 GDPR you can ask a controller to delete your personal data, for example when the purpose has ended, you withdrew consent or you objected to the processing. The company must answer your request within one month (in complex cases it can extend by two months). It may refuse for listed reasons, such as legal retention duties; then it should say which data it keeps and why. A simple letter or email is enough.

advertising_objection.title: Advertising: you can object to the use of your data for direct marketing
advertising_objection.summary: Under Article 21 GDPR you can object to processing based on legitimate interest, and for direct advertising the objection has to be respected. You can object informally by letter or email, and in the same message ask for deletion of the data. Verbraucherzentrale Niedersachsen offers a template. After the objection the company must stop sending you advertising.

dashcam_rules.title: Dashcam: usable as evidence in an accident case, but constant recording is not allowed
dashcam_rules.summary: In a decision of 15 May 2018 (VI ZR 233/17) the BGH allowed dashcam recordings as evidence in a civil accident lawsuit, but it also made clear that permanent, event-independent recording of traffic violates data protection law. Data protection authorities accept at most short, event-related recordings (for example triggered by an accident) that are overwritten otherwise. Publishing recordings is a separate problem.

fixed_term_prior_job.title: Fixed term without reason: not possible if you worked for the same employer before
fixed_term_prior_job.summary: A fixed-term contract without an objective reason is allowed for at most two years and can be extended up to three times within that period. It is not allowed if you were already employed by the same employer before, and the Federal Labour Court has held that even a gap of eight years does not automatically remove this ban (BAG 7 AZR 733/16). A previous student job at the same company can therefore matter. An invalid fixed term can lead to a permanent contract; the three-week period for a claim applies.

advertising_calls_consent.title: Advertising calls: only with your prior consent, fines up to 300,000 euro
advertising_calls_consent.summary: Advertising calls to consumers are only allowed with your prior express consent, and that includes existing customers. You can withdraw consent at any time. The Bundesnetzagentur can fine companies up to 300,000 euro, and a hidden or faked number is its own offence; it fines only calls to consumers, not to businesses. Report unwanted calls with the complaint form, ideally with date, time, number and caller. Typical sources of 'consent' are competitions.

paypal_friends_family.title: Buying second-hand: never pay with PayPal Friends & Family
paypal_friends_family.summary: A common scam on classified sites is a seller (or buyer) pushing you to pay by PayPal 'Friends and Family', claiming it is cheaper and faster. This option has no buyer protection, so if the item never arrives the money is gone. Pay only with 'goods and services' to get PayPal's buyer protection, never enter card data on links sent by the other side, and be careful with pressure and unusual requests. Consumer centres warn against this trick.

patient_file_copy.title: Patient file: you may see it and get a first copy free of charge
patient_file_copy.summary: Under § 630g BGB you can ask your doctor or hospital for prompt access to your complete patient file, without giving a reason, and you can ask for copies. The European Court of Justice ruled in October 2023 (C-307/22) that the first copy must be free of charge because of the GDPR, even though the BGB talks about costs. Further copies can be charged. Access can be limited for significant therapeutic reasons or rights of third parties. Consumer centres provide a template letter.

wohngeld_household_member.title: Housing benefit for a student sharing a home with someone who could not get BAföG
wohngeld_household_member.summary: The benefit is calculated for the whole household. A BAföG-eligible student is normally excluded, but there is an entitlement if at least one household member could not claim BAföG or similar support in principle, for example a partner, a child of a single parent or the parents of a student. Local offices decide the individual case.

wohngeld_application_timing.title: Housing benefit is paid from the month your application arrives; students need a BAföG rejection first
wohngeld_application_timing.summary: If the benefit is granted it is paid retroactively from the month in which the application arrived at the office, but processing often takes several weeks. As a student you first need a BAföG application and the rejection notice. A rejection only because you, your partner or your parents earn too much does not open up the benefit.

leave_germany_six_months.title: Leaving Germany for more than six months can end your residence permit
leave_germany_six_months.summary: A residence permit expires by law if you leave Germany and do not come back within six months, or within a longer period the Ausländerbehörde has set. It does not lapse the day you leave, but after the period ends, and an expired permit cannot be revived. If you plan a long semester abroad, apply for the longer period before you leave, or at the latest before the six months run out, and tell the office about your plans. Leaving for reasons that are not temporary can end the permit earlier. Exceptions exist, for example for some visas.

bridge_part_time.title: Temporary part-time (Brückenteilzeit): one to five years, then back to your old hours
bridge_part_time.summary: Since 2019 employees can ask to reduce their hours for a fixed period of one to five years and then return to the earlier working time. Conditions: you have worked for the employer for more than six months and the employer has more than 45 employees (in firms up to 200 staff a quota limits how many people can use it). The employer can refuse for operational reasons, which it must prove. During the period you cannot shorten or extend it or return early without agreement.
keywords: reduce hours then return full time

parental_leave_dismissal.title: Dismissal protection during parental leave starts at registration, at most eight weeks before
parental_leave_dismissal.summary: From the moment you register parental leave (Elternzeit), but at the earliest eight weeks before it begins, your employer cannot dismiss you without the permission of the competent labour authority. A dismissal without that approval is void, and the three-week period to go to the labour court still runs. The protection ends with the leave. If you want to quit yourself at the end of parental leave, a special notice period of three months applies, even if your contract says longer.

bnpl_risks.title: Buy now, pay later is a short-term loan: pay on time or fees and credit trouble follow
bnpl_risks.summary: Buy now, pay later (Klarna, PayPal and similar) means you get the goods now and pay later or in instalments. The payment is postponed, not cancelled, and consumer centres warn that it makes overspending easy, with fees or interest if you are late or choose instalments. Defaults can be reported and hurt your credit record. A press report says stricter consumer credit rules apply from April 2026, including BNPL and small interest-free instalment deals. Check what you owe before ordering and compare with simple invoice purchase.

studierendenwerk_counselling.title: Studierendenwerk counselling is free, confidential and can be anonymous
studierendenwerk_counselling.summary: Studierendenwerke offer psychological and social counselling for students, from exam stress to personal crises, and also advice on student finance, disability and international students. The counselling is free of charge, confidential and can be anonymous. Some places charge a small one-off registration fee (one Bavarian office names 10 euro), and cooperating centres may cover a limited number of sessions, so check your local Studierendenwerk. In an acute crisis the Telefonseelsorge (0800 1110111, 0800 1110222 or 116 123) is free at any hour.

cc_licence_attribution.title: Creative Commons licences: credit the author, link the licence and say what you changed
cc_licence_attribution.summary: A Creative Commons licence lets you share and adapt the work as long as you follow its terms. For CC BY you must name the author, link to the licence and state whether you made changes; commercial use is allowed. 'NC' forbids commercial use, 'ND' means you may not publish an edited version, and 'SA' means adaptations must be shared under the same licence. The licence does not cover other rights, such as personality or data protection rights of people in a picture. Always check the exact licence version.

gop_orientation_exam.title: Orientation exam (GOP): usually one retake, failing again can end the programme
gop_orientation_exam.summary: Many Bavarian degree programmes have a Grundlagen- und Orientierungsprüfung (GOP) in the first semesters. At FAU, for example, GOP-relevant exams can only be repeated once and failing the second attempt ends that subject. Exams you do not take in time can count as failed. The exact deadlines and the number of attempts are in your own Prüfungsordnung, so check it and talk to the study office before the deadline, and see the rules on illness and hardship if something got in the way.

tax_id_lost.title: Lost your tax ID: request it again free of charge from the Bundeszentralamt für Steuern
tax_id_lost.summary: The 11-digit Steuer-ID is assigned automatically and stays the same for life; you do not apply for it. It appears on your tax assessment, your Lohnsteuerbescheinigung and often on your payslips. If you cannot find it, you can have it sent again through the online form of the Bundeszentralamt für Steuern (BZSt) or by letter. It is free and arrives by post, not by email. Do not mix it up with the Steuernummer of your local tax office.

travel_vaccination_cost.title: Travel vaccinations: health funds pay only in some cases, ask before you get vaccinated
travel_vaccination_cost.summary: Statutory insurance pays the vaccinations recommended by the STIKO and for trips caused by work or training. Vaccinations for private holidays usually have to be paid by yourself, unless your fund offers them as a voluntary benefit (Satzungsleistung), and the rules differ between funds. Ask your fund before the vaccination, and expect to pay first and send in the invoice. Some vaccinations need several doses, so plan early.

racial_profiling_ruling.title: Police ID checks based on skin colour are unlawful (racial profiling)
racial_profiling_ruling.summary: The Higher Administrative Court of North Rhine-Westphalia ruled on 7 August 2018 (5 A 294/16) that an identity check by the federal police at a railway station was unlawful because skin colour was part of the reason. Skin colour may only play a role if the police can show specific indications, for example about crimes committed by a certain group, which they did not. The case shows you can challenge a check in court afterwards. Information only; speak to an advice centre about your own situation.

oral_exam_record.title: Oral exams: a record must be kept and signed by the examiners
oral_exam_record.summary: A university oral exam has to be documented in a record (Protokoll). It lists the essential parts of the exam and the result, but it is not a word-for-word transcript of questions and answers, and it is signed by the examiner and the second person present (Beisitzer). Oral exams are usually held by at least one examiner and a knowledgeable assessor. Details such as the duration and the number of examiners depend on your Prüfungsordnung.

google_fonts_warning.title: Website: Google Fonts loaded from Google can cause GDPR trouble, host them locally
google_fonts_warning.summary: In January 2022 the Landgericht München I (3 O 17493/20) held that loading Google Fonts dynamically from Google servers transmits the visitor's IP address to the USA without consent and awarded 100 euro damages. This led to a wave of mass warning letters, and in March 2023 the same court (4 O 13063/22) found the warning campaign abusive and denied claims. The simple fix for your portfolio website is to host the fonts locally. If you receive such a letter, do not pay in panic and get advice.

temp_agency_equal_pay.title: Temp agency work: equal pay after nine months
temp_agency_equal_pay.summary: Agency (Leiharbeit/Zeitarbeit) workers are entitled to the same pay as comparable permanent staff of the client company after nine uninterrupted months at the same client (AÜG § 8). A sector collective agreement may deviate only during the first nine months. Separately, the maximum assignment is 18 months, and a gap of more than three months resets that 18-month clock.

police_certificate_fee.title: Certificate of good conduct (Führungszeugnis): cost and fee waiver
police_certificate_fee.summary: A Führungszeugnis costs 13 euro and can be requested online from the Bundesamt für Justiz (with an eID) or at the registration office. People without means or volunteers can apply for a fee waiver with proof. The requesting employer decides how old the certificate may be; three months is common.

deregister_leaving_germany.title: Deregistering when you leave Germany
deregister_leaving_germany.summary: You only have to deregister (Abmeldung) if you move abroad, give up a second home, or have no new home in Germany. It must be done within two weeks after moving out, and can be done up to one week before. A move within Germany needs no deregistration.

erasmus_grant_amount.title: Erasmus+ study grant: amount and top-up
erasmus_grant_amount.summary: The Erasmus+ monthly grant for a semester abroad currently lies between 540 and 600 euro depending on the destination country, according to one university. Students with fewer opportunities can apply for an extra 250 euro per month. Your international office pays it out and sends a grant agreement first.

dooring_bike_accident.title: Cyclist hit by an opening car door (dooring)
dooring_bike_accident.summary: Drivers must take the utmost care when opening a door. In a first-instance ruling of 2 August 2022 (LG Köln, 5 O 372/20, not yet final at the time of the article) a cyclist got full compensation: when a collision happens right when a door opens, there is a presumption that the driver is at fault. The court said cyclists only need about 50 cm distance to parked cars. Individual cases can differ.

id_card_fee_2026.title: ID card fee and validity in 2026
id_card_fee_2026.summary: Since 7 February 2026 a German ID card costs 46 euro for applicants over 24 (valid 10 years) and 27.60 euro for under 24s (valid 6 years). A provisional ID costs 10 euro. German citizens from 16 must have an ID card or a valid passport. An expired ID cannot be extended, you apply for a new one.

lawyer_first_consultation_cap.title: Lawyer's first consultation: fee cap for consumers
lawyer_first_consultation_cap.summary: If you are a consumer, a lawyer may charge at most 190 euro plus VAT (about 226.10 euro) for a first consultation unless you agreed otherwise. For further advice the cap is 250 euro plus VAT. Employees asking about employment issues count as consumers.

tenant_self_disclosure_questions.title: Landlord questionnaire: which questions are allowed
tenant_self_disclosure_questions.summary: In a tenant self-disclosure (Mieterselbstauskunft) landlords may ask about job, income and household size. Questions about religion, party membership, health or family planning are not allowed. You must answer allowed questions truthfully, and false answers to them can cost you the contract or the tenancy. An untrue answer to a question that was not allowed has no legal consequences, according to several legal guides.

public_employer_disabled_interview.title: Severely disabled applicants: interview invitation at public employers
public_employer_disabled_interview.summary: Public employers must invite severely disabled applicants to an interview (SGB IX § 165 sentence 3), unless the applicant obviously lacks the professional qualification. If they skip the invitation, discrimination is usually presumed and compensation under the AGG can follow. The duty applies only to public employers. A church body under public law is not one, so it does not have to invite (BAG, 25 Jan 2024, 8 AZR 318/22).

early_loan_repayment_fee.title: Repaying an instalment loan early: fee cap
early_loan_repayment_fee.summary: For an ordinary consumer loan with a rate fixed at signing, the bank may charge a prepayment penalty (Vorfälligkeitsentschädigung) of at most 1 percent of the amount repaid early, or 0.5 percent if no more than a year remains. If the contract's information on term, termination or how the fee is calculated is inadequate, the bank loses the claim entirely. Contracts signed from 20 November 2026 fall under the new consumer credit rules, so check the date on yours.

bottle_deposit_return.title: Returning deposit bottles and cans
bottle_deposit_return.summary: Most shops must take back empty one-way deposit bottles and cans with the deposit logo and refund the 25 cent deposit, even if you bought them elsewhere. A shop may limit this to the material it sells (a can-only shop need not take plastic bottles), and shops under 200 square metres, such as kiosks and petrol stations, only need to take back the brands they sell. If the machine cannot read the container, staff must accept it by hand. Reusable bottles only need to be taken back if the shop sells that type, and they must be intact.

rent_guarantee_alternative.title: Rent guarantee instead of cash deposit (parents or insurer)
rent_guarantee_alternative.summary: Landlords may ask for at most three months' net rent as security. A parental guarantee is also capped at that level, and a guarantee and a cash deposit together may not exceed it. A landlord does not have to accept a bank or insurer guarantee. Parents who guarantee for a student stay liable even after the student starts earning, and there is no right to be released from the guarantee.

reminder_fees_limit.title: Reminder fees: only real costs, and the first reminder is free
reminder_fees_limit.summary: There is no fixed legal amount. A creditor may only charge the costs a reminder actually causes, and only once you are in default, so the reminder that first puts you in default cannot be charged. The Federal Court of Justice ruled in 2019 (VIII ZR 95/18) that a flat 2.50 euro reminder fee in an energy supplier's terms was not allowed, and fees like 10 euro have been struck down. Pay the invoice itself and ask for proof of the cost behind any fee.

kindergeld_study_abroad.title: Child benefit while studying abroad
kindergeld_study_abroad.summary: Kindergeld generally continues for a child studying in another EU or EEA country. Outside the EU/EEA the child must keep its residence in Germany. For a stay of about one year, Kindergeld usually continues. A longer stay can end the German residence, as the Lower Saxony Finance Court held (5 K 168/17, 7 Jan 2020), at least if the child does not spend its free time mainly at the parents' home. Short visits of two or three weeks a year are generally not enough. Keep proof, such as flight tickets.

employer_email_phone_monitoring.title: Employer checking your work email and phone
employer_email_phone_monitoring.summary: If private use of the company laptop or email is banned, the employer may check compliance, but only by spot checks, not permanent monitoring. If private use is allowed or tolerated, the employer counts as a telecoms provider and private emails fall under telecommunications secrecy, and connection data may only be recorded with your consent. Checking the content of private emails is generally excluded unless there is an initial suspicion of a crime or serious breach of duty. Total surveillance is generally disproportionate. Systems that can monitor behaviour need the works council's co-determination (BetrVG § 87). The source article dates from 2020.

wear_and_tear_not_tenant.title: Normal wear and tear: you do not pay for it
wear_and_tear_not_tenant.summary: Changes or deterioration of the flat that come from normal use under the lease are not the tenant's responsibility. A landlord cannot charge you for ordinary wear, such as slightly worn flooring or small marks from everyday living. Damage beyond normal use is different, and disputes are usually about which of the two it is.

landlord_damage_claims_six_months.title: Landlord's damage claims expire six months after you return the flat
landlord_damage_claims_six_months.summary: A landlord's claims for damage or deterioration of the flat expire six months after he gets the flat back. The six months start on the day of return. If the landlord's claim to get the flat back has itself expired, his damage claims expire with it.

tenant_expense_claims_six_months.title: Your claims for expenses or removing fixtures expire six months after the lease ends
tenant_expense_claims_six_months.summary: A tenant's claims to be repaid for expenses on the flat, or to be allowed to take away something he installed (for example shelves or a lamp fitting), expire six months after the tenancy ends. So raise such claims in good time.

rent_due_if_you_cannot_use_room.title: You still pay rent if you cannot use the flat for personal reasons
rent_due_if_you_cannot_use_room.summary: A tenant who cannot use the flat for a reason that lies with himself (for example a semester abroad or an internship in another city) is not freed from paying rent. The landlord has to credit what he saves and any benefit he gets from using the flat otherwise, for example by letting it to someone else. If the landlord has given the flat to a third party and cannot give you the use, you do not have to pay rent for that time.

landlord_duty_to_maintain.title: The landlord must keep the flat in a usable condition, you pay the agreed rent
landlord_duty_to_maintain.summary: The landlord must hand over the flat in a condition suitable for the agreed use and keep it in that condition during the tenancy. He also bears the costs and burdens that rest on the property itself. The tenant must pay the agreed rent.

landlord_notice_longer_after_five_years.title: Landlord's notice period grows by 3 months after 5 and after 8 years
landlord_notice_longer_after_five_years.summary: For the landlord the notice period increases by three months after five years and by another three months after eight years since the flat was handed over. Together with the basic three months this means six and nine months. Notice has to be given by the third working day of a month to end at the end of the month after next. An agreement that is worse for the tenant is invalid.

temporary_use_shorter_notice.title: Flats let for temporary use only: a shorter notice period can be agreed
temporary_use_shorter_notice.summary: For housing that is let only for temporary use, the parties may agree on a shorter notice period. Outside that case, agreements that are worse for the tenant than the statutory notice rules in § 573c Abs. 1 and 3 are invalid.

health_hazard_immediate_termination.title: Flat that seriously endangers your health: you can end the lease immediately
health_hazard_immediate_termination.summary: A tenant has an important reason for immediate termination if using the flat is linked to a considerable danger to health. This also applies if he knew about the condition when signing or did not use his rights before. When the reason is a breach of the landlord's duty, a reasonable deadline to fix it or a warning (Abmahnung) normally has to come first, unless that obviously would not help.

termination_reason_must_be_stated.title: Immediate termination of a flat lease must state the reason in the letter
termination_reason_must_be_stated.summary: When a lease on a flat is ended immediately for an important reason, the reason that leads to the termination has to be stated in the termination letter. A letter that gives no reason does not meet this requirement.

immediate_termination_important_reason.title: Immediate termination: only for an important reason, usually after a warning
immediate_termination_important_reason.summary: Both landlord and tenant can end a lease immediately only for an important reason, meaning that continuing until the normal end cannot reasonably be expected after weighing all circumstances, including fault, and both sides' interests. If the reason is a breach of a duty under the lease, a deadline to fix it or a warning (Abmahnung) normally comes first. That is not needed if it would obviously not help, if special reasons justify immediate termination, or in cases of rent arrears under § 543 Abs. 2 Nr. 3.

overstaying_agreed_or_local_rent.title: Not moving out on time: the landlord can charge agreed or local rent
overstaying_agreed_or_local_rent.summary: If the tenant does not return the flat after the lease has ended, the landlord can demand, for the time the flat is withheld, compensation equal to the agreed rent or the rent that is usual in the area for comparable flats. Claiming further damage is not excluded.

overstaying_further_damages_limited.title: Late return of a flat: further damages only if it is your fault
overstaying_further_damages_limited.summary: For a flat, the landlord can claim further damage beyond the compensation for late return only if the flat was not returned because of circumstances the tenant is responsible for. Even then the damage is compensated only as far as fairness requires. This does not apply if the tenant gave notice.

landlord_lock_change_forbidden.title: Landlord changing your locks or cutting you out of the flat is forbidden self-help
landlord_lock_change_forbidden.summary: Taking away someone's possession against their will, or disturbing it, is unlawful (verbotene Eigenmacht) unless a statute allows it. For a tenant this means a landlord may not change the locks, remove your things or block your access to push you out, even if you owe rent. He needs a court judgment and a bailiff for an eviction.

possessor_self_help_flat.title: What you may do if someone unlawfully takes or disturbs your possession
possessor_self_help_flat.summary: A possessor may use force to fend off unlawful interference with his possession. If a movable item is taken, he may take it back from the culprit caught in the act or pursued. For land, he may regain possession by removing the wrongdoer, but only immediately after the dispossession. The text speaks of land (Grundstück), so whether this carries over to a rented flat is a question for a lawyer, and delay ends the right.

tenant_hardship_objection_replacement_fl.title: Termination can be objected to if no reasonable replacement flat can be found
tenant_hardship_objection_replacement_fl.summary: A tenant can object to a landlord's termination and ask for the tenancy to continue if ending it would be a hardship for him, his family or his household that cannot be justified even considering the landlord's interests. A hardship also exists if suitable replacement housing cannot be found on reasonable terms. This does not apply where the landlord has grounds for immediate termination.

hardship_only_reasons_in_letter_count.title: Only the reasons named in the termination letter count in the hardship weighing
hardship_only_reasons_in_letter_count.summary: When the court weighs the landlord's interests against your hardship, only the reasons stated in his termination letter are considered. The exception is reasons that arose later. An agreement that is worse for the tenant than these rules is invalid.

objection_form_and_deadline.title: Objection to termination: text form, at least two months before the lease ends
objection_form_and_deadline.summary: Your objection to a landlord's termination must be declared in text form, for example a letter or email, and on request you should give the reasons without delay. It must reach the landlord at least two months before the tenancy ends. If it comes later, the landlord can refuse to continue the tenancy.

objection_late_at_first_hearing.title: Landlord did not tell you about the objection right: you can still object in court
objection_late_at_first_hearing.summary: If the landlord did not point out in good time before the objection deadline that you may object, and the form and deadline for it, you can still declare your objection at the first hearing of the eviction lawsuit.

agg_indirect_discrimination.title: Indirect discrimination: a neutral-looking rule that hits one group harder
agg_indirect_discrimination.summary: Indirect discrimination exists when rules, criteria or procedures that look neutral put people with a protected characteristic at a particular disadvantage compared with others. It is only allowed if the rule serves a legitimate aim and the means are appropriate and necessary. The protected grounds are race or ethnic origin, sex, religion or belief, disability, age and sexual identity.

agg_harassment_definition.title: Harassment linked to a protected ground counts as discrimination
agg_harassment_definition.summary: Unwanted behaviour connected to a protected ground (such as origin, religion, disability, age, sex or sexual identity) is discrimination if it aims at or results in violating your dignity and creating an environment of intimidation, hostility, degradation, humiliation or insult. Racist or demeaning jokes and remarks at work or at university can fall under this.

agg_compensation_cap_three_salaries.title: Compensation for a discriminatory rejection is capped at three monthly salaries
agg_compensation_cap_three_salaries.summary: If you were rejected for a job because of discrimination, you can claim appropriate money compensation for the non-material harm. If you would not have been hired even with a fair selection, the compensation may not exceed three monthly salaries. The claim must be asserted in writing within two months.

agg_everyday_claims_remove_and_damages.title: Discriminated against as a customer or tenant: stop it, damages and compensation
agg_everyday_claims_remove_and_damages.summary: If you are discriminated against in everyday dealings such as shops, services, or renting, you can demand that the disadvantage is removed and, if more is feared, sue to stop it happening again. The other side must compensate material damage unless it is not responsible, and you can ask for appropriate money for non-material harm. An agreement that departs from the ban cannot be relied on against you.

agg_everyday_two_month_deadline.title: Everyday discrimination claims (shops, services, renting): two months
agg_everyday_two_month_deadline.summary: Claims after discrimination in everyday dealings must be asserted within two months. Unlike job claims, the law does not require this to be in writing, but writing it down helps you prove it. After the deadline you can only claim if you were not at fault for missing it.

agg_housing_social_mix_exception.title: Landlords may justify different treatment to keep a balanced resident mix
agg_housing_social_mix_exception.summary: When renting out housing, different treatment is allowed in view of creating and keeping socially stable resident structures, balanced settlement structures and balanced economic, social and cultural conditions. Landlords sometimes cite this to justify refusals, but it is an exception and it does not allow turning someone down simply because of origin.

rent_increase_waiting_period.title: Rent increase to the local comparative rent: only after 15 months without change
rent_increase_waiting_period.summary: A landlord can demand your consent to a rise up to the local comparative rent only if the rent has been unchanged for 15 months at the date the increase is meant to take effect. The request itself can come at the earliest one year after the last increase. Raises for modernisation or running costs do not count towards this.

rent_increase_comparative_rent_six_years.title: Local comparative rent: rents agreed or changed in the last six years
rent_increase_comparative_rent_six_years.summary: The local comparative rent (ortsübliche Vergleichsmiete) is formed from the usual rents in the municipality or a comparable one for flats of similar type, size, fittings, condition and location, including energy quality, that were agreed or changed in the last six years. Flats where the rent is fixed by law or a subsidy are left out.

rent_increase_only_by_law_or_agreement.title: A landlord can raise the rent only by agreement or in the ways the law lists
rent_increase_only_by_law_or_agreement.summary: During the tenancy the parties can agree on a higher rent, including a step rent or an index rent. Otherwise the landlord can demand an increase only under §§ 558 to 560 (local comparative rent, modernisation, running costs), unless an increase was excluded by agreement or by the circumstances. A deal that is worse for the tenant is invalid.

rent_increase_landlord_has_three_months_.title: If you do not agree to a rent increase, the landlord must sue within three more months
rent_increase_landlord_has_three_months_.summary: If you do not agree to the increase by the end of the second calendar month after receiving the request, the landlord can sue for your consent. He has to file the lawsuit within three further months. If his request had formal defects, he can fix them in the court case, and you then get the same consideration period again.

step_rent_rules.title: Step rent (Staffelmiete): in writing, in euros, at least a year apart
step_rent_rules.summary: A step rent must be agreed in writing, and each rent or each increase has to be given as an amount of money. The rent must stay unchanged at least one year between steps, and during the step rent no increase under §§ 558 to 559b is possible. The tenant's right to terminate can be excluded for at most four years from signing.

course_materials_15_percent.title: Course materials: teachers may share up to 15 percent of a published work
course_materials_15_percent.summary: For teaching at educational institutions such as universities, up to 15 percent of a published work may be copied, distributed and made available online for non-commercial purposes, for the course participants and for examiners. This is why professors upload chapters of books to the learning platform but not whole books. Splitting a work into parts to get around the limit is not allowed.

withdrawal_no_reason_send_in_time.title: Withdrawal from an online purchase needs no reason, and sending it in time is enough
withdrawal_no_reason_send_in_time.summary: The withdrawal does not have to give any reason, and it is enough that you send it within the deadline. The period is 14 days. After a withdrawal, what each side received has to be given back without delay.

withdrawal_missing_info_twelve_months.title: Withdrawal right ends at the latest 12 months and 14 days after the start date
withdrawal_missing_info_twelve_months.summary: The right to withdraw from a distance or doorstep contract expires at the latest twelve months and fourteen days after the point in time when the period would have begun. If the seller never gave proper information about the right to withdraw, the 14 days do not start running, so the right can last well beyond two weeks until that outer limit.

gdpr_answer_deadline_extension.title: A company must answer your data request within one month; two more months only with notice
gdpr_answer_deadline_extension.summary: The controller has to act on your request, for example for access or erasure, without delay and at the latest within one month of receiving it. The period can be extended by a further two months only where necessary because of complexity or the number of requests, and the controller must tell you about the extension and the reasons within the first month.

student_permit_needs_admission.title: Student residence permit: you need admission from the university first
student_permit_needs_admission.summary: A residence permit for full-time study is granted once the state or state-recognised university, or a comparable institution, has admitted you. The stay also covers preparatory measures such as a language course or Studienkolleg and a compulsory internship. A language certificate is only required if the admission procedure did not test your language and the preparatory measure will not provide it.

student_permit_two_years_validity.title: Student permit: normally two years at first issue and at each renewal
student_permit_two_years_validity.summary: The residence permit for study is valid for two years as a rule, both when first issued and when renewed, and it should not be shorter than one year. If the study lasts less than two years, it is issued only for that time. It is extended if the study purpose has not been reached yet but can still be reached within a reasonable time, and the university may be asked about this.

student_permit_nine_months_new_admission.title: Lost your place through no fault of your own: up to nine months to find another university
student_permit_nine_months_new_admission.summary: Before a student permit is withdrawn, revoked or shortened because of reasons you are not responsible for, you must be given up to nine months to apply for admission at another institution. This can matter if a university closes or your admission falls away without your fault.

student_permit_part_time_or_language_wit.title: Permit also possible for part-time study, language course or prep internship without admission yet
student_permit_part_time_or_language_wit.summary: A student permit can also be granted if you are admitted on a condition not tied to a preparatory course, to a part-time programme, or conditionally with a Studienkolleg place you cannot prove yet. It can also be granted for a language course without university admission, or for a preparatory internship the company has committed to. In the internship case the permit allows the internship.

language_course_permit_20_hours.title: Permit for a language course (not preparing for study): work up to 20 hours a week
language_course_permit_20_hours.summary: A residence permit can be granted for a language course that is not preparation for studies. Such a permit allows you to work up to 20 hours per week. Permits for a student exchange or for school attendance do not allow gainful employment.
